instructions:
You are connected to the DreamFactory service "snap".
Available database APIs: ordersdb, crm
## Getting Started
IMPORTANT: Call `ordersdb_get_semantics` FIRST. It returns the approved business definitions for the data in a few KB: warnings about traps in the data, what terms like "current" mean, and metrics and verified queries with the exact tool and arguments to run them. When a question matches one, run it as given. Otherwise call `ordersdb_get_data_model` before composing any query of your own.
The data model provides in a single ~10-20KB response:
- Every table with all columns (name, type, primary key, foreign keys)
- Foreign key references showing how tables connect
- Structural patterns you MUST handle correctly:
  * HIERARCHIES: Self-referencing FKs (e.g. dept.parent_dept_id → dept.dept_id) mean
    records form a TREE. You must use recursive traversal to find ALL descendants,
    not just direct children. Aggregate metrics must roll up through ALL levels.
  * JUNCTION TABLES: Many-to-many relationships via intermediate tables.
- Row counts per table
## Tool Usage Guide
Argument names are snake_case (table_name, count_only, include_count); camelCase is accepted too. Unknown arguments are rejected, never ignored.
All database tools are prefixed with the API name (e.g., db_get_tables, mysql_get_table_data).
The same verb on every database shares the same parameters — only the prefix changes.
Use the list_apis tool to see all available APIs.
1. `ordersdb_get_semantics` - START HERE. Business definitions: warnings, glossary, metrics and verified queries with runnable arguments (small).
2. `ordersdb_get_data_model` - Condensed schema with columns, FKs, and patterns, for queries the definitions do not cover.
3. `ordersdb_get_api_spec` - OpenAPI spec with query syntax hints. Use compact=true (default).
4. `ordersdb_get_table_data` - Query data with filter, order, limit, offset, fields, related
5. `ordersdb_aggregate_data` - Compute SUM/COUNT/AVG/MIN/MAX in ONE call (no manual pagination needed)
6. `ordersdb_get_table_schema` - Full schema for a single table (if you need more detail)
7. `ordersdb_create_records` / `update_records` / `delete_records` - CRUD operations
8. `ordersdb_get_stored_procedures` / `call_stored_procedure` - Stored procedure access
9. `ordersdb_get_stored_functions` / `call_stored_function` - Stored function access
## Query Syntax Quick Reference
- Filter: `field=value`, `field>10`, `field LIKE %text%`, `field IN (1,2,3)`, `field BETWEEN 1 AND 10`, `field IS NULL`
- IMPORTANT: Use field names exactly as they appear in the schema — do NOT add quotes, brackets, backticks, or URL-encoding around field names. Spaces in field names are valid as-is. Example: `Production Day=2026-03-16` (NOT `[Production Day]`, NOT `"Production Day"`, NOT `Production%20Day`)
- Combine filters: `(field1=value1) AND (field2>value2)`, `(f1=v1) OR (f2=v2)`
- Order: `field ASC`, `field DESC`, `field1 ASC, field2 DESC`
- Fields: select specific columns to reduce response size
- Related: include related records via foreign keys (e.g., `related=parent_table_by_fk_field`)
- Pagination: use `limit` and `offset`, set `include_count=true` for total count
- Counting: use `count_only=true` to get just the count without data
- Aggregation: use `ordersdb_aggregate_data` for SUM/COUNT/AVG/MIN/MAX — it pushes computation to the database server
- Max page size: 1000 records. Always paginate for tables with more rows.
## Key Data Modeling Hints
- When a table has a column referencing ITSELF (self-referencing FK), it forms a tree/hierarchy.
  Example: dept.parent_dept_id → dept.dept_id means departments are nested.
  You MUST recursively traverse to aggregate child data into parent totals.
- When you see amount + paid_amount columns, compute outstanding = amount - paid_amount.
  An invoice with status "paid" but paid_amount < amount still has an outstanding balance.
All tools operate against the DreamFactory REST API using the authenticated user session.

tools.name: discover_services
tools.title: Discover Services
tools.description: Discover which DreamFactory services and operations YOU (the calling agent) are permitted to access, based on your assigned role. Returns the role-filtered service catalog with the operations (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) allowed on each. Call this first to learn your boundaries before querying any data.

tools.name: request_access
tools.title: Request Access
tools.description: Request access you do not currently have. Creates a pending request for human approval and notifies administrators via alerts. Provide the service names and operations you need plus an optional reason. You will NOT get access immediately — an administrator must approve it, after which a fresh scoped key is issued.

operations.description: Operations needed: any of GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE.

note.description: Why you need this access (shown to the approving admin).

tools.name: list_apis
tools.title: List Available APIs
tools.description: List the database and file services in this connection with their category and tool-name prefix. Lighter than discover_services, which also reports the HTTP verbs your role permits on each service; call that when you need to know what you may write.

tools.name: all_get_tables
tools.title: Get Tables from All Databases
tools.description: Table names from every connected database in one call, keyed by service name. Use it when you do not know which database holds the data; for one database call get_tables, and for columns and relationships call get_data_model.

tools.name: all_find_table
tools.title: Find Table Across All Databases
tools.description: Look up one table name in every connected database and return its full schema from each database that has it. Use it when a table could live in several services. Returns foundIn (the services that have it) plus per-service schema or error.

table_name.description: Exact table name to look for.

tools.name: all_get_stored_procedures
tools.title: Get Stored Procedures from All Databases
tools.description: Stored procedure names and parameters from every connected database, keyed by service; empty for services without procedures. For a single database call get_stored_procedures.

tools.name: all_get_stored_functions
tools.title: Get Stored Functions from All Databases
tools.description: Stored function names and parameters from every connected database, keyed by service; empty for services without functions. For a single database call get_stored_functions.

tools.name: all_get_resources
tools.title: Get Resources from All Databases
tools.description: Resource groups (_table, _schema, _proc, _func) exposed by every connected database, keyed by service. Use it only to compare what each service offers; all_get_tables is the lighter call when you just need tables.

tools.name: ordersdb_get_api_spec
tools.title: ordersdb: Get API Spec
tools.description: [ordersdb] OpenAPI 3.0 spec for this database: endpoint paths, query-parameter syntax and, with tables=true, every table. Use it when you need exact filter/order syntax or endpoint details; get_data_model is the cheaper call for planning queries. compact=true (default) returns the token-efficient form.

resource_name.description: Get spec for a specific table/resource only

tables.description: Include full table and field details

tools.name: ordersdb_get_semantics
tools.title: ordersdb: Get Business Definitions
tools.description: [ordersdb] CALL FIRST. Approved business definitions for this database: what terms like "current", "active" or "headcount" mean in the data, metrics and verified queries with the exact tool arguments to run them. Small; follow these definitions instead of guessing.

tools.name: ordersdb_get_data_model
tools.title: ordersdb: Get Data Model
tools.description: [ordersdb] Condensed model of every table: columns (name/type/FK), row counts, hierarchies, junction tables. Call get_semantics first; use this to plan any query the business definitions do not already answer. On larger databases the first call returns an index; pass tables for the details you need.

tables.description: Only these tables, with samples and enumerations (plus their relationships). Omit for all.

detail.description: Full detail for every table even on a large database (default: index above 12 tables)

samples.description: Sample rows per table (default 1; 0 for none)

templates.description: Include query templates (default: only when no catalog query exists)

refresh.description: Bypass the cached model and rebuild it from the database (slow on large schemas).

tools.name: ordersdb_get_tables
tools.title: ordersdb: List Tables
tools.description: [ordersdb] Table names only, the cheapest schema call. Use it to confirm a table exists; get_data_model also returns columns and relationships for every table.

tools.name: ordersdb_get_table_schema
tools.title: ordersdb: Get Table Schema
tools.description: [ordersdb] Full definition of ONE table: columns with types, nullability and defaults, primary and foreign keys, and the related-table aliases usable in get_table_data related=. Use it after get_data_model when one table needs closer inspection. get_table_fields returns only the column list and get_table_relationships only the relationship graph.

table_name.description: Exact table name as returned by get_tables or get_data_model.

tools.name: ordersdb_get_table_data
tools.title: ordersdb: Get Table Data
tools.description: [ordersdb] Read rows from one table with filter/order/limit/offset. Returns 50 rows unless limit is set (max 1000); meta.next tells you when there are more. count_only=true returns just the count. For SUM/COUNT/AVG/MIN/MAX/GROUP BY use aggregate_data — this tool cannot aggregate.

table_name.description: Exact table name from get_tables or get_data_model.

fields.description: Columns to return (default: all). Fewer columns means a smaller response.

filter.description: SQL-like WHERE clause: field=value, field>10, field LIKE %text%, field IN (1,2), field IS NULL; combine with AND/OR in parentheses, e.g. (status=open) AND (amount>100). Use bare field names, no quotes or brackets around them.

offset.description: Rows to skip before the first returned row; combine with limit to page.

limit.description: Max records per request (default 50, server max 1000). Use with offset to paginate.

order.description: Sort clause: "field ASC" or "field DESC", comma-separated for several, e.g. "created DESC, id ASC".

continue.description: Rarely needed on reads: continue past per-row errors in a batch instead of failing the whole request.

related.description: Include related records via FK (e.g. "parent_table_by_fk_field"). Check relationships in the data model.

count_only.description: Return only the record count, no data. Use this instead of COUNT() in fields.

include_count.description: Include total record count in response metadata alongside data.

include_schema.description: Append the table schema to the response (adds size; prefer get_table_schema).

ids.description: Primary-key values to fetch directly, instead of a filter.

tools.name: ordersdb_create_records
tools.title: ordersdb: Create Records
tools.description: [ordersdb] Insert one or more rows into a table. Returns the primary key of each new row (or the columns named in fields). Not idempotent: repeating the call inserts again. To change existing rows use update_records.

table_name.description: Exact table name from get_tables or get_data_model.

records.description: Rows to insert, one object per row keyed by column name. Omit auto-increment keys.

fields.description: Columns to return for each created row (default: primary key only).

related.description: Related-table alias whose nested records inside each row should be created too, e.g. "orders_by_customer_id".

continue.description: On a per-row error keep inserting the remaining rows and report each failure, instead of stopping at the first.

rollback.description: On any per-row error undo the rows this call already inserted (all or nothing).

tools.name: ordersdb_update_records
tools.title: ordersdb: Update Records
tools.description: [ordersdb] Patch existing rows: only the columns present in each record change. Target rows one of three ways: records that each carry the primary key; ids plus a single record applied to every id; or filter plus a single record applied to every match. Returns the primary keys (or fields) of the rows changed.

table_name.description: Exact table name from get_tables or get_data_model.

records.description: Column/value pairs to apply. One object per row when each carries its primary key; a single object when targeting by ids or filter.

fields.description: Columns to return for each updated row (default: primary key only).

related.description: Related-table alias whose nested records inside each row should be updated too.

ids.description: Primary-key values of the rows to patch with the single record.

filter.description: SQL-like filter (same syntax as get_table_data) selecting the rows to patch with the single record.

continue.description: On a per-row error keep updating the remaining rows and report each failure, instead of stopping at the first.

rollback.description: On any per-row error undo the rows this call already changed (all or nothing).

tools.name: ordersdb_delete_records
tools.title: ordersdb: Delete Records
tools.description: [ordersdb] Permanently delete rows selected by ids or filter; there is no undo. A call with neither ids nor filter is refused unless force=true, which empties the whole table. Returns the primary keys of the deleted rows.

table_name.description: Exact table name from get_tables or get_data_model.

ids.description: Primary-key values of the rows to delete.

filter.description: SQL-like filter (same syntax as get_table_data) selecting the rows to delete.

force.description: true deletes EVERY row in the table when no ids or filter are given. Never set it casually.

fields.description: Columns of each deleted row to return (default: primary key only).

related.description: Related-table alias whose records should be included in the response for each deleted row.

continue.description: On a per-row error keep deleting the remaining rows and report each failure, instead of stopping at the first.

rollback.description: On any per-row error restore the rows this call already deleted (all or nothing).

tools.name: ordersdb_get_table_fields
tools.title: ordersdb: Get Table Fields
tools.description: [ordersdb] Column list for one table: name, type, length, nullable, default, primary/foreign-key flags. Lighter than get_table_schema, which also returns constraints and related tables; get_data_model already lists these columns for every table.

table_name.description: Exact table name from get_tables or get_data_model.

refresh.description: Bypass the schema cache and re-read from the database.

tools.name: ordersdb_get_table_relationships
tools.title: ordersdb: Get Table Relationships
tools.description: [ordersdb] Relationships of one table: foreign keys in and out, self-referencing hierarchies (parent_id-style trees) and junction tables for many-to-many. Use it to pick the related= alias for get_table_data; get_data_model summarizes the same relationships for every table.

table_name.description: Exact table name from get_tables or get_data_model.

refresh.description: Bypass the schema cache and re-read from the database.

tools.name: ordersdb_get_stored_procedures
tools.title: ordersdb: List Stored Procedures
tools.description: [ordersdb] List the stored procedures this database exposes, with their parameter names and types, callable through call_stored_procedure. Empty on databases without procedures (e.g. SQLite).

tools.name: ordersdb_call_stored_procedure
tools.title: ordersdb: Call Stored Procedure
tools.description: [ordersdb] Execute a stored procedure by name with named parameters and return its result sets and output parameters. Procedures can modify data: check what the procedure does (get_stored_procedures) before calling it.

procedure_name.description: Procedure name exactly as listed by get_stored_procedures.

parameters.description: Input parameters keyed by parameter name.

wrapper.description: Key under which to wrap the returned result set in the response.

returns.description: Declared data type of the procedure's scalar return value, e.g. "integer", when the database cannot infer it.

tools.name: ordersdb_get_stored_functions
tools.title: ordersdb: List Stored Functions
tools.description: [ordersdb] List the stored functions this database exposes, with their parameter names and return types, callable through call_stored_function. Empty on databases without functions.

tools.name: ordersdb_call_stored_function
tools.title: ordersdb: Call Stored Function
tools.description: [ordersdb] Execute a stored (scalar or table-valued) function by name with named parameters and return its value. Functions usually only read, but treat one as able to write unless you know otherwise.

function_name.description: Function name exactly as listed by get_stored_functions.

parameters.description: Input parameters keyed by parameter name.

returns.description: Declared data type of the return value, e.g. "integer", when the database cannot infer it.

tools.name: ordersdb_get_database_resources
tools.title: ordersdb: List Database Resources
tools.description: [ordersdb] List the resource groups this database service exposes (_table, _schema, _proc, _func) with their member names. Use it to check whether a service has procedures or functions at all; for table work use get_tables or get_data_model.

as_access_list.description: Return every resource/verb combination the current role may call (for checking permissions).

include_access.description: Add the HTTP verbs the current role may use on each resource.

fields.description: Resource properties to include (default: name only).

tools.name: ordersdb_aggregate_data
tools.title: ordersdb: Aggregate Data
tools.description: [ordersdb] THE ONLY WAY to SUM/COUNT/AVG/MIN/MAX/GROUP BY: pushes the aggregation to the database and returns one row per group. Always pass group_by when the question is per category. Grouped results return 100 groups unless limit is set; the response says when there are more. Do not use get_table_data for aggregation; use it for raw rows instead.

filter.description: Filter rows before aggregating (same syntax as get_table_data)

limit.description: Max groups to return (default 100, max 5000). Narrow with filter when truncated.
